sections.h2: Who sends the Miami Beach tax bill?
sections.html:
One combined bill arrives from the Miami-Dade County tax collector, and the city of Miami Beach is only one line on it. The property appraiser sets value and says on its homepage that it neither mails bills nor collects money.

The Census Bureau lists 7.69 square miles of land for Miami Beach and 81,594 people for mid-2025. Packing that many residents onto a barrier island is why individual parcels can land on different taxing lines of the county chart.

sections.h2: What is the Miami Beach millage rate for 2026?
sections.html:
The county's 2026 adopted millage chart lists Miami Beach at 5.8060 mills for city operations plus 0.2693 for city debt service. One mill is one dollar of tax for every thousand dollars of taxable value.

The chart prints two Miami Beach lines. The first totals 18.6681 mills across every taxing authority. The second adds 0.7364 and totals 19.4045. Your tax bill or the appraiser's parcel search shows which line your folio falls under.

  • The city line is only part of the bill. County, school, regional, fire and rescue, library and Children's Trust amounts sit on top of it.
  • The chart is titled as adopted rates, so these figures are final for the 2026 roll.
  • The county roll was certified on October 16, 2026, before any Value Adjustment Board changes.

sections.h2: Is the Miami Beach rate high compared with nearby cities?
sections.html:
The county chart puts Miami Beach near the middle. Its 5.8060 city mills compare with 5.5590 in Coral Gables, 7.1080 in Miami and 3.7743 in Surfside, while Bal Harbour lists 2.5132 and Key Biscayne 2.8708.

Totals differ again because some rows carry extra lines. Surfside totals 18.4824 mills, Bal Harbour 17.2213 and Key Biscayne 15.4636, against 18.6681 on the first Miami Beach line. Compare totals, not just the city line, when you weigh the island against a neighboring town.

sections.h2: Who lives in Miami Beach, according to the Census?
sections.html:
The 2020 count was 82,890 people, against 87,779 in 2010, and the mid-2025 estimate sits 1.6 percent under the 2020 base. Land density works out to 10,774.7 residents per square mile.

More than half of residents (52.9 percent) were born abroad. About four in five had stayed at the same address over the previous twelve months, so turnover is modest.

  • Commutes average 26.7 minutes each way.
  • Per capita income is $75,054, above the household median because households are small.
  • Lodging and restaurant sales reached about $3.78 billion in 2022, a sign of how much the local economy leans on visitors.

sections.h2: How many people own versus rent in Miami Beach?
sections.html:
Owners live in 40.9 percent of housing units, in the five-year survey. Those owned homes carry a median value of $556,700, and renters pay $1,826 in median gross rent.

The city counts 41,600 households averaging 1.95 people, and residents 65 and older are 18.8 percent of the population, so most sellers sit outside the age-based relief programs. Household income has a median of $72,856 in 2024 dollars.

With under half of units lived in by owners, a Miami Beach seller often faces investors and second-home shoppers. Whether you had a homestead exemption on January 1 does more to shape your tax picture than any other line.

sections.h2: What are the key tax dates for Miami Beach owners?
sections.html:
Florida runs one tax cycle per calendar year, and Miami Beach follows the same schedule as every other city.

Annual tax calendar that governs a Miami Beach parcel
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date
March 1Exemption and classification filing deadline
AugustTRIM notice mailed
25 days after the noticeValue petition due with the clerk
NovemberTax bills go out
November to February4, 3, 2 and 1 percent discounts
April 1Unpaid taxes turn delinquent

Dates taken from the state revenue department's taxpayer page.

sections.h2: How does homestead work for a Miami Beach house?
sections.html:
A homestead exemption of up to $50,000 applies, and you file Form DR-501 with the property appraiser by March 1. The first $25,000 reaches school taxes too, while the second $25,000 touches only assessed value above $50,000 and skips school taxes.

  • The home must be your permanent residence as of January 1.
  • Renting the unit or moving out ends the exemption.
  • Under Save Our Homes, annual increases are limited to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. The state chart lists a 2.7 percent cap for 2026.
  • A sale resets the property to just value on the next January 1.

That reset is why a buyer's first full bill in Miami Beach can look very different from yours.

sections.h2: Can I take my homestead savings to a new house if I move from Miami Beach?
sections.html:
Often yes, through portability. You must set up the new homestead within three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old one, not three years after the sale date. File Form DR-501T together with the DR-501 by March 1.

The state statute describes the transfer as the lesser of $500,000 or the gap between just value and assessed value on the old home. The statute page notes amendments that first apply to the 2027 roll, so confirm the current cap with the appraiser before you plan around a number.

Owners who cannot pay a full bill can ask the tax collector about a homestead deferral on Form DR-570, due March 31, or an installment plan requested by May 1.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid tax if I sell a Miami Beach house?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax is paid off from your sale proceeds. The title agent requests a payoff from the tax collector and settles the year's share at the table.

After April 1, the county can sell a certificate on the debt, and a holder may seek a tax deed once two years have passed. A homestead property opens at a bid that includes half the latest assessed value.

Clearing a balance before listing keeps the sale clean. The tax collector runs 13 locations, online payment and mobile offices, so options exist.

sections.h2: Which office takes a Miami Beach deed for recording?
sections.html:
The Miami-Dade clerk's county recorder office, 20 NW 1st Avenue, Suite 5.246, takes Miami Beach deeds. Florida requires two witnesses on a deed, per section 689.01.

The clerk's page lists deed documentary stamps at 60 cents per $100, with a 45 cents per $100 surtax on transfers of real property other than a single-family residence. See the Miami-Dade records guide for the full fee list.

sections.h2: Who do I call with questions about a Miami Beach assessment?
sections.html:
The appraiser's downtown office is at 111 NW 1st Street, Suite 710, and it opens Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM. Phone 305-375-4712. A second branch serves the south end at 10710 SW 211 Street in Cutler Bay.

Bring your folio number, TRIM notice and any closing statement from your purchase. For a balance owed, call the tax collector.

faqs.q: Does Miami Beach send its own property tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The Miami-Dade County tax collector sends one combined bill that includes the city line of 5.8060 mills for operations plus 0.2693 for debt service.

faqs.q: When does a Miami Beach tax bill become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1 of the year after assessment. Before then, the November to February discounts of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent apply, and March is due at the full amount.

faqs.q: Can I keep my Save Our Homes cap if I sell?
faqs.a: The cap does not transfer with the sale, because a change of ownership resets value to just value. You may carry part of the benefit to a new Florida homestead through portability, which needs Form DR-501T by March 1 and a new homestead within three years.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 Miami Beach millage rate final?
faqs.a: Yes. The county chart lists adopted 2026 rates, with the city at 5.8060 mills. Individual parcels can fall on different lines, so check your own bill.

faqs.q: Who pays the doc stamps when I sell?
faqs.a: All parties to the deed are liable under state rules, regardless of which side agrees to pay. Your contract and title agent decide who actually pays.
